vivaQuestions.question: Why does an AVL tree provide faster lookups than a standard Binary Search Tree?
vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: An AVL tree strictly enforces height balancing where heights of two child subtrees differ by at most one, guaranteeing O(log n) worst-case lookup rather than degenerating into O(n).

vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: The Halting Problem asks whether an arbitrary computer program with input will finish running or run forever. Alan Turing proved via diagonalization and contradiction that no universal algorithm can solve this for all program-input pairs.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the Bias-Variance tradeoff in machine learning?
vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: High bias leads to underfitting by oversimplifying assumptions. High variance leads to overfitting by being overly sensitive to training noise. The tradeoff seeks optimal model complexity minimizing total expected error.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the CAP theorem in distributed systems?
vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: A distributed data store can simultaneously provide at most two out of three guarantees: Consistency (every read receives the most recent write), Availability (every request receives a non-error response), and Partition Tolerance (system continues operating despite network partitions).

vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: A message digest produces a fixed-size cryptographic hash ensuring data integrity. A digital signature encrypts that digest with the sender's private key, providing authenticity, integrity, and non-repudiation.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is the computational complexity of FFT O(N log2 N) compared to O(N^2) for direct DFT?
vivaQuestions.sampleAnswer: Direct DFT requires N^2 complex multiplications. Radix-2 FFT exploits the periodicity and symmetry properties of twiddle factors (W_N^k) through recursive divide-and-conquer, reducing complex multiplications to (N/2)log2(N).
